Does a Term Supply Its Fourth Derivative?

Source: R/outer_gradient.R
answers_term_fourth.Rd

answers_term_third()'s question one order up, and read the same way: from the class the method is registered on, never from a list of class names.

Usage

answers_term_fourth(term)

Arguments

term

A built term.

Value

A single logical.

Details

The criterion's own second derivative reads a fourth order through the recursion, so a term that has written the third and not the fourth supplies an exact gradient and no exact Hessian. That is the state regime() is in: it implements neither, and a term implementing only the third would be answered here with FALSE and left to statmod_hess_stencil(), which is the same fallback its search already has.

See also

outer_gradient_ok(), statmod_structural_hess()
